newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA'S MACFARLANE SAYS GOVT SHOULD NOT PICK WINNERS.
newsitem.headline: RBA'S MACFARLANE SAYS GOVT SHOULD NOT PICK WINNERS.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Ian Macfarlane said on Tuesday the government should not pick growth areas as the economy adjusts to change.
"I find it hard to believe that the government would be better than the private sector at picking growth areas," Macfarlane told a business dinner here.
He said the government's main contribution should be to remove unnecessary obstacles to change, provide infrastructure, encourage saving and lift the quality of education.
Australia's conservative government is under pressure from business to take a more interventionist line on industry policy.
Lobby groups have pointed to Australia's unemployment rate, stuck at around 8.5 percent, as an incentive for the government to actively encourage investment in certain areas.
However, Macfarlane said the key to ensuring long-run growth was raising productivity, a goal which would require Australia to embrace change, however painful.
"I know this is a difficult message to give to a public which is growing tired of change, not all of it economic," he told the Australian Institute of Company Directors' dinner.
"But the alternative of stopping change is really not viable," he added.
"There is clearly a large role for government," he said.
"But we should always ask whether particular government initiatives are forward looking or whether they are protecting an existing industry or an existing privilege."
the main contribution to boosting productivity should be removing obstacles to change, not picking should focus on removing obstacles to economic change, not picking growth areas.
